films.title: Yanuni
films.year_scope: Original film year stated by its producer. The official full-film YouTube edition was published September 5, 2026.
films.credits: Directed by Richard Ladkani; producers Juma Xipaia, Leonardo DiCaprio, Anita Ladkani, Richard Ladkani, Jennifer Davisson and Phillip Watson.
films.publisher: Malaika Pictures / Leonardo DiCaprio official channel
films.synopsis: Juma Xipaia defends her people's Amazonian land while navigating leadership and motherhood. Family resilience meets threats from illegal mining and the struggle for Indigenous sovereignty.
films.availability: Full film on producer Leonardo DiCaprio's official YouTube channel. Location, account or provider restrictions may apply.
films.content_note: Discusses threats against Indigenous defenders, illegal mining and dangerous environmental enforcement operations.
films.perspective: Centers Juma Xipaia of the Xipaya people in Brazil, who is credited as both participant and producer. Instituto Juma identifies her as its founder. This film does not represent every Amazonian Indigenous community.

sources.title: About Us: Juma Institute And Juma Xipaia
sources.evidence: Juma Xipaia is an Indigenous leader belonging to the Xipaya people

sources.title: Yanuni: Official Full-Film Upload
sources.evidence: Released worldwide on Amazon Day, 5 September 2026.

films.accessibility_note: The publisher lists English, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish and Thai caption tracks, plus a Portuguese automatic track. Caption accuracy and synchronization have not been verified. Brief playback startup was checked; this is not a complete film review.
films.release_note: The producer lists the feature as 112 minutes. The official YouTube upload is 113m42s, including a 57-second trailer and introductory material; its runtime must not be substituted for every film edition.

films.title: Daughter of a Lost Bird | Indigenous Adoption
films.synopsis: An excerpt confronts Native child removal and forced assimilation within a film following Kendra and her mother as they reconnect with each other and Lummi heritage.
films.availability: Official 3m 20s excerpt page and transcript. PBS playback was unavailable when checked on 2026-10-16. The child-removal percentage is historical, not a present-day rate.
films.content_note: Child separation and historical racist language.

sources.title: Daughter of a Lost Bird | Indigenous Adoption

films.title: First Light
films.credits: Directed by Adam Mazo and Ben Pender-Cudlip; producer N. Bruce Duthu (Houma).
films.synopsis: Wabanaki experiences of child removal meet an effort in Maine to uncover the truth and pursue healing through a truth and reconciliation commission.
films.availability: The filmmaker offers free streaming for individual viewing and lists separate institutional licensing for public or school screenings. Regional playback was not tested.
films.content_note: Discusses forced child removal, cultural loss and family separation.
films.perspective: Centers Wabanaki people and child-welfare workers. The producer page explicitly identifies producer N. Bruce Duthu as Houma.

films.title: Dawnland
films.year_scope: PBS premiere year, also stated by the producer.
films.credits: Directed by Adam Mazo and Ben Pender-Cudlip; producer N. Bruce Duthu (Houma); senior advisor Chris Newell (Passamaquoddy).
films.synopsis: A Maine truth and reconciliation commission investigates the removal of Wabanaki children, opening difficult conversations about responsibility, family and cultural survival.
films.availability: The producer lists rental or purchase for individual viewing. Current free full-film playback was not established.
films.content_note: Discusses forced child removal, abuse and intergenerational harm.
films.perspective: The producer credits Houma, Passamaquoddy and other Native participants and advisors; this does not imply every filmmaker has Indigenous identity or every community endorses the film.

sources.title: Dawnland
sources.evidence: Rent or purchase for individual viewing

films.release_note: Full-film runtime differs from PBS broadcast player runtime. The producer explicitly lists 86-minute and54-minute versions.

films.title: Gather
films.credits: Directed by Sanjay Rawal; producers Sterlin Harjo and Tanya Meillier.
films.synopsis: Native food advocates reclaim food systems, knowledge and community relationships, connecting food sovereignty with cultural continuity and care for the land.
films.availability: The official page embeds a trailer and lists commercial viewing providers. Provider access, subscriptions and regional availability can change; full-film playback was not verified.
films.content_note: Discusses colonization and disruption of Native food systems.
films.perspective: An Indigenous-led First Nations Development Institute project. Its project page identifies Native team members and describes stories from Native people, without implying the director is Indigenous.

sources.title: Home | Gather Film
sources.evidence: growing Native American food sovereignty movement

sources.title: Watch | Gather Film
sources.evidence: The film is available on iTunes, Amazon, Vimeo on Demand, and Netflix.

films.title: Bring Them Home
films.credits: Narrated and executive produced by Lily Gladstone (Blackfeet/Nez Perce), as credited by PBS.
films.synopsis: Blackfoot community members work to return buffalo to tribal lands, linking ecological restoration with cultural renewal and the future of their communities.
films.availability: PBS lists the film as streaming and provides an ASL version. Availability may depend on region or provider conditions; no universal free-playback claim.
films.content_note: Discusses buffalo loss, colonial oppression and community healing.
films.perspective: Centers Blackfoot/Blackfeet community efforts. PBS explicitly identifies narrator and executive producer Lily Gladstone as Blackfeet/Nez Perce.

sources.title: Bring Them Home
sources.evidence: Bring Them Home is available to stream on pbs.org and the PBS app.

films.accessibility_note: The listed ASL version is1h18m53s. That is version-specific, so no unqualified feature runtime or production year is inferred from the PBS show page.

films.title: Inhabitants
films.credits: Co-directed by Costa Boutsikaris and Anna Palmer; producer/advisor Ben-Alex Dupris; Native impact producer Colleen Cooley.
films.synopsis: Five Native communities share approaches to land stewardship, from dryland farming and forest care to buffalo restoration and food systems in Hawaiʻi.
films.availability: The filmmaker links to Vimeo on Demand and iTunes and offers separate community screening routes. Current payment, region and playback conditions were not independently tested.
films.content_note: Discusses colonization, land disruption and climate impacts.
films.perspective: The official About page names a Tribal Advisory Board with Hopi, Native Hawaiian, Blackfeet, Karuk and Menominee participants; it identifies Ben-Alex Dupris as Colville and Colleen Cooley as Diné.

sources.title: About | Inhabitants
sources.evidence: representatives from each of the Tribes highlighted in the film

films.editorial_limit: The homepage contains unrelated template-like blog entries. Only the stable film synopsis, About credits and explicit official watch links support this entry; template entries are not used as reporting.

films.title: Lakota Nation vs. United States
films.credits: Directed by Jesse Short Bull and Laura Tomaselli.
films.synopsis: Lakota voices challenge dispossession and distorted representations, connecting the Black Hills with enduring community life, resistance and sovereignty.
films.availability: Official distributor trailer. This is not the full documentary. Regional playback and future platform availability can change.
films.perspective: Centers Lakota people and resistance. The retained metadata does not independently establish the identity of every filmmaker; none is inferred.

sources.title: Lakota Nation vs. United States (Open Captioning)
sources.evidence: Director Jesse Short Bull, Laura Tomaselli

sources.title: Lakota Nation vs. United States - Official Trailer | HD | IFC Films

films.historical_screening_note: The IFC Center page lists2023 screenings. These are historical events, not a current ticket or screening promise.

films.title: We Still Live Here - Âs Nutayuneân
films.synopsis: Wampanoag community members work to bring their language into new generations, joining archival documents, study and community determination.
films.availability: Official film information and credits. Current full-film streaming availability was not established; this link is not presented as a free full-film player.
films.content_note: Discusses language suppression and cultural recovery.
films.perspective: Follows Wampanoag language work involving Aquinnah and Mashpee communities. The credits state that Tribal-member interview opinions do not represent the Aquinnah government; no broader endorsement is implied.

sources.title: We Still Live Here | Independent Lens

films.title: Kanehsatake: 270 Years of Resistance
films.credits: Written and directed by Alanis Obomsawin.
films.synopsis: Filmed behind Kanien’kéhaka lines, this documentary follows the 1990 confrontation over a proposed development on Mohawk lands at Oka.
films.availability: Official NFB film and viewing page. NFB determines playback, rental and regional terms.
films.content_note: NFB warns that the film contains scenes of violence.
films.perspective: The publisher describes footage from behind Kanien’kéhaka lines during the standoff. No creator identity is inferred solely from that filming position.

sources.title: Kanehsatake: 270 Years of Resistance
sources.evidence: This work contains scenes of violence.

films.runtime_basis: Publisher JSON-LD gives PT1H59M. The separate collection endpoint returnedHTTP500; its more precise cached runtime was not adopted.

films.title: Birth of a Family
films.year_scope: NFB film-version year metadata, separate from upload date.
films.credits: Directed by Tasha Hubbard; written by Tasha Hubbard and Betty Ann Adam.
films.synopsis: Four Indigenous siblings separated through child-removal policies meet and piece together family history, building connections that years apart could not erase.
films.availability: Official NFB film and viewing page. Access may depend on territory or NFB conditions.
films.content_note: Discusses forced child removal, adoption and family separation.
films.perspective: Centers four Indigenous siblings rebuilding family relationships. No identity label for the director is inferred without a separate explicit biography.

sources.title: Birth of a Family
sources.evidence: their connection deepens, and their family begins to take shape.

films.runtime_basis: Publisher JSON-LD gives PT1H19M and film-version metadata gives2017. Its separate collection endpoint returnedHTTP500 and is not used as a successful receipt.

films.title: Uýra - The Rising Forest
films.credits: PBS lists Juliana Curi, João Henrique Kurtz, Lívia Cheibub, Martina Sönksen and Uýra Sodoma as filmmakers.
films.synopsis: In the Amazon, Uýra uses performance and shared knowledge to connect Indigenous youth with identity, place and the interdependence of people and the environment.
films.availability: Official PBS POV information and resources. Current full-film playback was not established; the page lists a 2023 PBS premiere, not a current event.
films.content_note: Discusses racism, transphobia and environmental harm.
films.perspective: The official synopsis explicitly centers Indigenous youth and ancestral knowledge in the Amazon. It does not by itself establish every filmmaker's identity.

sources.title: Uýra - The Rising Forest
sources.evidence: Uýra shares ancestral knowledge with Indigenous youth in the Amazon

films.runtime_basis: PBS lists60minutes and aSeptember25,2023 premiere. No production year is inferred from that broadcast date.

films.title: Blood Memory
films.synopsis: Sandy White Hawk reconnects with her Sicangu Lakota family and supports other Native adoptees returning to their communities.
films.availability: Official film information. Current full-film streaming or free access was not verified.
films.content_note: Family separation, abuse and adoption-related trauma.

resources.title: Colorado: Truth And Restoration
resources.text: People of the Sacred Land publishes its Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission reports on Colorado history and its recommendations for restoration. Read the research and the organization's own framing.

resources.title: Education That Continues
resources.text: People of the Sacred Land shares curriculum and virtual learning materials about American Indian history. These resources offer another way to stay with the subject beyond a film.
